Summary: 
The column argues that U.S. pressure on Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro is the centerpiece of a new hemispheric strategy by President Donald Trump. The author cites several U.S. actions: in August 2017 Trump asked the Oval Office why he could not simply invade Venezuela; in March 2020 the Department of Justice formally charged Maduro and associates with narco‑terrorism, offering a $15 million reward for information leading to his capture; the reward was later raised to $50 million. Three guided‑missile destroyers—USS Jason Dunham, USS Sampson and USS Gravely—were deployed off the Venezuelan coast as a warning. Maduro responded by accusing the U.S. of a coup attempt and mobilizing 4.5 million militiamen. The column also notes that Venezuela produced 886,000 barrels of oil per day in December 2024, according to OPEC, and that the designation of Venezuelan cartels as terrorist organizations changes the rules of engagement. The author urges Latin America to act with force, not merely observe, to protect its autonomy and ensure that changes in Venezuela are not dictated exclusively from abroad. Key quotes include: 'un cambio de régimen en Venezuela podría traer estabilidad y beneficios para la región', 'no puede depender únicamente de la Casa Blanca', and 'la región debe actuar con fuerza, no solo observar'.

Title: Efemérides 31 de Diciembre Venezuela

Summary: 
On December 31st, Venezuela celebrates various anniversaries, commemorations, and historical events. Some notable events include the death of John Wyclif, a translator, theologian, and reformer who is considered the spiritual father of the Husites and Protestants. George Marshall, a military leader, statesman, and politician, was born on this day in 1880. He is known for his leadership in the Second World War and for the Marshall Plan, which helped to rebuild Europe after the war. The first International San Silvestre de São Paulo race was held in 1925, and it has since become a traditional event in South America. Anthony Hopkins, a renowned actor, was born on this day in 1937. He is known for his iconic role as Hannibal Lecter in 'The Silence of the Lambs.' Donna Summer, a singer, songwriter, and actress, was born on this day in 1948. She is known as the 'Queen of Disco' and is famous for her hits in the 1970s and 1980s. The Avenida Bolívar in Caracas was inaugurated by President Carlos Delgado Chalbaud in 1949. The last episode of Renny Ottolina's show was broadcast on this day in 1973, marking his retirement from television. Boris Yeltsin resigned as President of Russia and was succeeded by Vladimir Putin in 1999. The United States officially transferred the administration of the Panama Canal to Panama in 1999, marking the end of a process that began with the Torrijos-Carter Treaties in 1977. Avensa, a major Venezuelan airline, ceased operations in 2004. The Walt Disney Company acquired Marvel Entertainment for approximately $4 billion in 2009, adding over 5,000 Marvel characters to its catalog. Venezuela closed the year with a record-high inflation rate of 130,060.20% in 2018, according to the Central Bank of Venezuela.
